privacy.lead: What we collect through this site, why, who helps us process it, and how to see, correct or delete your data.

toc.title: What we collect, form by form
Why we use it, and on what basis

parts: Genesis Hacks (“Genesis”, “we”, “us”) runs the website at www.genesishacks.com. Genesis connects companies with India's student hackathon and builder community. We curate brand partnerships with independent hackathons and run our own series, Hackers Occupied.

For the purposes of the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (the “DPDP Act”), Genesis Hacks decides why and how the personal data described here is used, so we are the Data Fiduciary for it. You are the Data Principal.
The short version.

We collect what you type into our forms so we can reply to you, we never sell it, analytics stay off unless you accept them, and you can ask us to see, correct or delete your data at any time by writing to

sections.title: What we collect, form by form

parts: We only collect what each form asks for. Fields marked optional on a form can be left empty.

items: Security and spam control. When you send a form we store a one-way, salted hash of your IP address and your browser’s user agent, so we can block repeated or automated submissions. We cannot turn the hash back into your IP address.
Server logs. Our hosting provider keeps short-lived technical logs (IP address, time, page requested) to run and protect the site.

Analytics, only with your consent. If you click Accept on the cookie banner, PostHog records the pages you visit, device type, approximate region and where you came from. If you click Reject, or do nothing, no analytics load.

parts: We do not ask for sensitive information such as financial details, health data or identity documents through this site. Please do not include them in a message or upload.

sections.title: Why we use it, and on what basis

parts: We use your personal data to:

items: reply to your message or enquiry and keep the conversation going;
assess sponsorship, partnership and collaboration requests and match them to events;
tell you about the event you registered interest in, such as Hackers Occupied Delhi;
consider crew applications;
issue certificates to registered participants;
keep the site secure and free of spam; and
with your consent, understand which pages are useful.

parts: Consent. Sending a form is a clear, affirmative act: you give us your data for the purpose shown on that form. Analytics run only on your separate consent through the cookie banner.

Legitimate uses. Some processing relies on the legitimate uses allowed by section 7 of the DPDP Act, for example using data you gave us voluntarily for the purpose you gave it, or keeping records a law requires us to keep.
We do not sell personal data, we do not use it for advertising, and we do not make automated decisions about you.
A small number of service providers (Data Processors) handle data on our behalf, under contract and only to provide their service to us:
Service providers that process personal data for Genesis Hacks

rows: Hosts the website and runs the server functions that receive forms
Database and private file storage for form submissions and uploaded decks
Team email and a working copy of form submissions
Sends the team a notification email when a form arrives (if enabled)
Optional analytics, only after you click Accept

parts: Some of these providers store data outside India. The DPDP Act allows this unless the Government of India restricts transfers to a particular country, and we will follow any such restriction.

We share your details with a sponsor or event partner only when you ask us to (for example, to make an introduction) or when you agreed to it on an event’s own registration form. If you register for an event on another platform, such as HackCulture or Luma, that platform’s privacy policy applies to the data you give it.
We may also disclose data if the law requires it, or to protect our rights or someone’s safety.

items: Enquiries (contact, partner, collaborate, crew applications, event interest): up to 24 months after our last exchange with you, then deleted.
Uploaded decks and files: up to 12 months, then deleted.
Certificate checks: not stored. The participant list itself is kept as one-way hashes of each registered email and phone pair.
Analytics: kept by PostHog in line with its retention settings, and only if you accepted.

parts: We delete data sooner if you ask us to and no law requires us to keep it, or once the purpose you gave it for is complete.
Under the DPDP Act you can:

items: ask for a summary of the personal data we hold about you and how we use it;
ask us to correct, complete or update it;
ask us to erase it;
withdraw your consent at any time;
have a grievance about our handling of your data addressed; and
nominate another person to exercise these rights for you if you die or become unable to.

parts: To use any of these rights, email
with the subject “Data request”. We reply
within 2 business days
. We may ask you to confirm it is really you before we act.
If you are not satisfied with our response, you can complain to the Data Protection Board of India.

Withdrawing consent is as easy as giving it. Use Cookie settings at the bottom of any page to change your analytics choice, or email us to withdraw consent for anything else. Withdrawal does not affect processing that already happened.
The site stores a few small items in your browser:

items: Your consent choice (essential), so we remember whether you accepted or rejected analytics.
Intro seen (essential, this browser session only), so the opening animation plays once.
PostHog cookies and storage, only after you click Accept.

parts: The DPDP Act treats anyone under 18 as a child, and processing a child’s data needs verifiable consent from a parent or lawful guardian.

items: The forms on this site are meant for adults. If you are under 18, please ask a parent or guardian to contact us for you.
Registration for student events such as Hackers Occupied needs verifiable consent from a parent or guardian for any participant under 18.
We do not track children, monitor their behaviour or show them targeted advertising.
If we learn that we hold a child’s data without that consent, we delete it. Parents and guardians can write to
at any time.
The whole site runs over HTTPS.
Form submissions and decks are stored in a private database and a private storage bucket that the public cannot read. Only our server functions hold the access key, and it never reaches your browser.
IP addresses are stored only as salted hashes.
Access to submissions is limited to the Genesis team members who need it.

parts: No system is perfectly secure. If a breach affects your personal data, we will inform you and the Data Protection Board of India as the DPDP Act requires.

terms.lead: The rules for using genesishacks.com, sending us enquiries and taking part in Genesis events.

parts: These terms apply when you use www.genesishacks.com (the “site”), which is run by Genesis Hacks, India (“Genesis”, “we”, “us”). By using the site you agree to them. If you do not agree, please do not use the site.
In plain words.
Use the site honestly, do not try to break it, and know that a sponsorship or event place is only confirmed once we both sign a separate written agreement or you receive a confirmed registration.
The site lets you:

items: learn what Genesis does for companies and for student builders;
read about our own series, Hackers Occupied, and events we have run or partnered on;
send us a sponsorship, partnership, collaboration or crew enquiry;
register interest in upcoming events such as Hackers Occupied Delhi; and
download a certificate if you took part in Hackers Occupied Pune.

parts: Each event has its own registration process, rules and code of conduct, which apply alongside these terms when you take part.
When you use the site, you agree not to:

items: send false, misleading or someone else’s details through a form;
use the certificate tool to look up, or try to guess, other people’s details;
upload files that contain malware or that you have no right to share;
try to break, overload, scan or get around the site’s security;
scrape the site in a way that harms its performance; or
use the site for anything unlawful.

parts: We may block access or ignore submissions that break these rules.
Sending a form does not create a contract. Prices, packages and deliverables for a sponsorship or partnership are agreed separately, in writing, before any payment or commitment.
You confirm that what you send us is accurate and that you are allowed to share it, including any deck or document you upload. We treat sponsor decks as confidential and handle them as our
describes.
We reply to genuine enquiries within 2 business days.

Event details on the site, such as dates, venues, tracks and team sizes, can change. Where we mark something as tentative (for example, the dates of Hackers Occupied Delhi), it is a plan, not a promise. Figures marked as projections are estimates, not results.
Photos and videos are taken at Genesis events and may appear on this site and our social channels. If you appear in one and want it removed, email
and we will take it down.

Names and logos of other companies belong to their owners. When a brand appears on the site, it means the brand sponsored or took part in an event that Genesis ran or partnered on. It does not mean that brand endorses Genesis. If you represent a brand and want its name or logo changed or removed, email us.

The site’s text, design, photos and the Genesis name and logo belong to Genesis or are used with permission. You may share links to the site and quote short passages with credit. Please ask before reusing anything else.

Certificates are issued only to registered participants, using the email and phone they registered with. A certificate confirms participation in the named event. Altering a certificate or presenting someone else’s as your own is not allowed, and we may confirm or deny a certificate’s authenticity if asked.
The site links to other services, such as event registration platforms and social networks. We do not control them, and their own terms and privacy policies apply when you use them.
We work to keep the site accurate and available, but we provide it “as is”, without guarantees that it will always be error-free or online.

To the extent the law allows, Genesis is not liable for indirect or consequential loss arising from your use of the site. Nothing in these terms limits liability that cannot be limited under Indian law.
These terms are governed by the laws of India, and disputes about them are subject to the jurisdiction of the courts in India.
We may update these terms. When we do, we change the date at the top of this page. Continuing to use the site after a change means you accept the updated terms.
